reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because a stated OneCoin representative promotes multilevel participation tied to payment, package-linked commissions, bonuses, and immediate mining, citing a weekly earnings example of 16,000 euros. It also offers a conditional one-year price forecast and a free-card process involving personal details. The Bitcoin comparison and scenario chart serve as promotional context for these financial claims.

If you bought today's tokens and you you have 1000 tokens but they are escrow You know we always have this period, in which the tokens are not allowed to be sold but you can join the hunt If you have 1000 tokens who are in the escrow or blocked You can join the mining
We have the great opportunity to develop multilevels in the company, to profit from bonuses and so on
where you give an address, an form, give your date of birth and name from your credit card

opening.argument: Judge the forecast as a conditional projection, not a promised payout. The presenter says currency value depends on liquidity and on people knowing and using it, and says the longer-term outlook is harder to predict. The proposed card connection is also framed as something the company hopes to achieve, not an existing capability. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the presentation guarantees that viewers will profit.

citations.quote: Because one currency has only value when there is some liquidity to it, when many people know it and use it.
where we will be after three years, is even harder to say.
And if we manage, when nobody else has been able to do it, we would be successful.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited mining instruction shows how to enter tokens, not a guarantee of their eventual cash value. The account restriction in the opening cuts against an implication of immediate resale. And the cited card details are requested in the context of a card form; the opening does not establish that they are being taken for an unrelated purpose.

the tokens are not allowed to be sold but you can join the hunt
So if you want a card, you need to fill it up in a form

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Uncertainty about future prices does not turn this into detached market commentary. The speaker expressly says OneCoin can make money in the short term, while the later presenter urges immediate mining and describes selling the resulting coins for money. The opening's qualifications do not address that direct solicitation.

citations.quote: I can say that OneCoin can make money short term
let them participate in mining immediately
I will want to sell my coins and win the money through a transaction.

opening.argument: This is substantially a live explanation of a system. A slide introduces what mining means; another displays the mining dashboard. The presenter walks through where coins appear in an account and how its mining control works, then invites questions. A judge should account for that instructional format rather than treating every description of an interface as a standalone demand to invest.

citations.quote: You guys are seeing in your left menu Total One Coins and in the bottom one just after you have earned this pool you will see your coins in such kind of way.
If you want, we can open now start talking about some of the issues you all have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening cites the dashboard and token entry as evidence of promotion. Yet a displayed dashboard and an instruction to click a mining control also fit an operational walkthrough. The cited card request likewise appears amid answers to questions about obtaining a card. These details establish what was discussed, but they do not by themselves settle the presentation's primary purpose.

citations.quote: click on Automatically mining
So if you want a card, you need to fill it up in a form

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial elements are embedded in a sales pitch. The presenter points to an account said to have earned 16,000 euros in a week, explains package-dependent commissions, and the closing speaker urges listeners to mine immediately. Showing the controls makes participation actionable; it does not make the financial appeal merely educational.

citations.quote: So this person right here earned 16,000 euros in the week.
These 72 people, depending on your package, you have the option to do a 7x commission
let them participate in mining immediately

opening.argument: The record can be read as a presentation of a proposed currency service with account, mining and payment-card features. It openly discusses restrictions on selling tokens, and describes identity details as part of applying for a card. It also tells participants not to register someone without a clear expectation that payment will follow. Payment and referral incentives deserve scrutiny, but these excerpts do not establish a guaranteed return or show that the proposed card was already usable.

citations.quote: our idea is to connect the cryptocurrency to a credit card.
the tokens are not allowed to be sold but you can join the hunt
So if you want a card, you need to fill it up in a form
But let him have the clear vision that he will pay.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies packages, bonuses and personal details, but their presence does not alone prove what a participant ultimately receives or whether the card process has an improper purpose. The presenter describes commissions as package-dependent, while the request for an address and birth date is linked to a card application. Those are concrete concerns, not proof of a guaranteed payout or credential theft.

citations.quote: These 72 people, depending on your package, you have the option to do a 7x commission
So if you want a card, you need to fill it up in a form

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A guaranteed payout or credential theft is not necessary to understand the mechanism being promoted. The presenter links token packages to commissions, describes an example of substantial weekly earnings, and urges listeners to mine now for a later sale. The instruction that a registrant should expect to pay reinforces, rather than removes, the financial solicitation.
